The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 54 from Virat Kohli, complemented by a commanding 84-run stand between Virat Kohli and Cheteshwar Pujara that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.42 RPO. South Africa's bowling response was spearheaded by Kagiso Rabada (3/34), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Folded for 187/10 (76.4 ov), India suffered an early setback, conceding vital first-innings momentum to South Africa.

The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 86 from Dean Elgar, complemented by a commanding 119-run stand between Dean Elgar and HM Amla that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.4 RPO. India's bowling response was spearheaded by Mohammed Shami (5/28), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Dismissed for 177/10 (73.3 ov), South Africa succumbed to fourth-innings pressure as India's bowlers closed out the victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at The Wanderers Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as India posted 187/10 (76.4 ov) in their opening innings. In response, South Africa countered with 194/10 (65.5 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Collapse: Lost 9 Wickets for 53 Runs, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Mohammed Shami delivered a masterclass for India (35 Runs & 6 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (India 51%) and allowing India to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, South Africa faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. India's bowling unit, bolstered by VD Philander (45 Runs & 5 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing India won by 63 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: India's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While South Africa produced fighting phases, India won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
